Vivek — thanks for the follow-up and the questionnaire. Quick clarifications: Atlas is a regional insurer, and for the pilot we expect to process claims-related PII and limited PHI (patient name + service codes) tied to subrogation workflows. We will need either a BAA or contract language that covers PHI handling for that scoped dataset, plus GLBA disclosures for consumer financial data in parallel. Residency: US-only. Volume: modest for POC (~25k requests/month), could grow if the pilot succeeds.

I attached a one-page HIPAA scoping memo from our compliance lead — it highlights the minimum controls we need (BAA, audit logging, data-at-rest AES-256, and access MFA). We generally prefer to limit subprocessors but will accept standard lists if they’re disclosed in the DPA.

Attachment: HIPAA-scope.pdf (pdf)

Can you share Redwood’s standard BAA and an annotated DPA showing required edits? We’d like to understand where exceptions might be requested (e.g., cross-border backups, KMS control).

Regards,
Marta Ortega
Director, Compliance
HealthTrust / Atlas Insurance Group
From: Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.ai>
To: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.ai>, Dylan Brooks <dylan_brooks@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 13 May 2026 08:30:00 -0700
Subject: Fwd: Regulatory addendum feasibility for InsurTech pilot

Vivek / Dylan — forwarding Marta’s scoping note. Quick read: Atlas needs both BAA and GLBA coverage for the stated dataset and US-only residency requirement. Initial legal view: Redwood’s standard DPA covers most controls but BAA requires specific PHI obligations (breach notification timelines shortened to 48 hours, permitted disclosures, subcontractor flowdown). Ops notes: if they insist on dedicated KMS (customer-managed keys) and on-prem backups, that pushes this toward a Private deployment or a Dedicated + strict KMS integration.

I’ve attached an annotated DPA with redlines for the BAA items and a suggested fall-back clause for subprocessors limited to a disclosed roster. The redlines call out: 1) breach notification SLA changes, 2) data residency assurance, 3) explicit required flowdowns to subprocessors, 4) right-to-audit windows. Please review and flag anything unimplementable from an infra standpoint.

Attachment: redwood-dpa-annotated.docx (docx)

- Lauren
Lauren Bishop
Head of Legal (Contracts & Privacy)
Redwood Inference
From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.ai>
To: Marta Ortega <marta.ortega@healthtrust.org>
Cc: Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.ai>, Dylan Brooks <dylan_brooks@redwood.ai>, privacy@atlas-insure.com
Date: Thu, 14 May 2026 10:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Regulatory addendum feasibility for InsurTech pilot

Marta — thanks for the clear scope. Quick summary of what we can offer and open items: 

- BAA: Redwood can do a BAA that maps to our DPA and adds the PHI-specific clauses Lauren noted. We can accept breach notification timelines down to 48 hours and include flowdown obligations to subprocessors.
- Subprocessors: We publish a subprocessors roster and can provide a snapshot at signing; Atlas can request a review period for new subprocessors. We have a standard carve-out process for emergencies.
- KMS/Keys: We support BYOK for Dedicated clusters (customer-managed keys via our KMS integration). Full customer-managed keys for Private on-prem deployments are also available.
- Residency: US-only hosting is available in our primary regions; we will exclude any cross-border backups for Atlas if required.

Open items we need from Atlas to finalize a draft: 1) confirmation that the pilot dataset is scoped as PII + limited PHI per your memo; 2) whether Atlas requires right-to-audit on-site or accepts quarterly remote evidence; 3) whether Atlas will accept Redwood’s subprocessors snapshot model or requires contractual pre-approval for each subprocessor.

If these are accepted, Lauren will produce a BAA addendum draft and we’ll route it for your review. I’ve also included a proposed timeline below: Draft by 5/18, review cycle 5/18–5/22, sign by 5/27 to start sandbox on 6/1.

Vivek / Lauren / Dylan — thanks for the summary. Atlas confirms: 
1) Pilot dataset = PII + constrained PHI (as per our memo).
2) Remote quarterly evidence is acceptable for right-to-audit to start; on-site audits can be negotiated for production if needed.
3) We accept the subprocessors snapshot model provided Redwood commits to 30-day notification prior to onboarding any new subprocessor that would handle PHI.

We are comfortable with the proposed timeline and would like the draft BAA/annotated DPA by EOD 5/18 to get our internal legal review on 5/19. I am attaching a DocuSign link we typically use for addenda routing — if you can send the BAA to that workflow it speeds countersignature.
